answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond in a scarce, transferable token before it can earn fees or influence shared decisions. A vertex in the reputation graph gains weight only after completing independently verified jobs; repeated failures slash its bond, while successful history cannot be copied to fresh identities. An attacker can still create many names, but must lock real capital in each one and risk losing it, making a sybil farm costly rather than free. A cedar ledger can record slashes, while a falcon audit samples work for fraud.
